correctness.rationale: For A=e1 the scalar sketched Hessian W has a scaled chi-square density proportional to w^(ell/2-1) at zero. The r-th power moment of 1-eta/W is finite exactly for r<ell/2, including the sharp logarithmic divergence at equality. Conditioning on every possible Bernoulli refresh partition yields independent blocks; the all-retention event of probability (1-p)^(k-1)>0 proves the exact 2qk cutoff, and bounded block size proves sufficiency. The iid 2nd-moment multiplier computed from exact inverse gamma moments is 2/(ell-2) at eta=(ell-4)/ell. For p>0 the Markov refresh chain is stationary ergodic, log|1-eta/W| is integrable, and Jensen plus the iid second moment gives a finite negative almost-sure Lyapunov exponent independent of p. Periodic-block SLLN supplies its comparison. A standalone exact rational checker passed 1275 identity/boundary tests; the proof, not these tests, establishes infinite moments and asymptotic limits.

originality.rationale: The defining IHS analysis uses independent iteration sketches. Lacotte and Pilanci distinguish fully fixed versus fully independent fresh sketches and prove an exact mean-square rate only under their independence hypothesis; their conditional fixed-sketch bounds do not imply unconditional finite moments when Bernoulli retention is introduced. Wang, Ouyang and Xu treat sequentially nested Gaussian sketches and a different double-sketch gradient/Hessian update, not the Hessian-only Bernoulli holding schedule. The new asserted statement is the exact refresh-run integrability clock jointly with p-invariant almost-sure contraction and deterministic capped-reuse boundary, not the known iid rate or the generic inverse-chi-square formula. Plausible unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed literature may already discuss Bernoulli-held Gaussian Hessian inverse tails or the equivalent Markov-run integrability condition.
The moment computation is a specialization of known inverse-gamma integrability; priority rests on the joint refresh-design theorem, not on a new inverse-gamma identity.
Existing broad high-probability theory is compatible with the rare-event divergence and cannot be treated as contrary evidence.

value.rationale: The refresh policy is an explicit computational design choice in iterative Hessian sketching. The theorem proves that an arbitrarily small chance of retaining a Gaussian preconditioner produces an infinite unconditional mean-square error at a finite horizon, despite retaining the same negative almost-sure exponent. Its deterministic periodic-reuse comparison provides a sharp and actionable sketch-width/budget condition for finite moments. This is a structural separation between typical behavior and moment-based guarantees, not a generic one-step textbook deduction, a fabricated speedup, or a finite census.
